posts.text: Status-6 On November 19, 2026, US President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Putin held the first-ever trilateral meeting of the leaders of the three countries. The summit took place at Kylin Villa (Qilin Shanzhuang) in Shenzhen… sonable to make such far-fetching conclusions. Yalta brought together wartime allies (US, UK, USSR) whose armies were defeated a common enemy. They negotiated occupation zones, borders, the shape of the postwar order, and the UN with the concrete power to enforce outcomes. The Shenzhen meeting was a first-time trilateral among strategic competitors (not allies) on the sidelines of an economic summit. In 1945, the Big Three could largely dictate terms because of military realities on the ground. Today, middle powers and alliances retain significant agency. Ukraine continues to fight, while European states and NATO remain involved in the ongoing processes. So I don't think we can make a parallel here. tweet

⚡️ Iran: No obligation justifies sacrificing national security for safeguards 📌 London, IRNA — The Islamic Republic has strongly warned the IAEA Board of Governors about the potential use of its nuclear information for any acts of aggression against Iran. Iran’s Permanent Mission to International Organizations in Vienna wrote on its X account on Thursday, “The information collected by IAEA may serve safeguards, but will surely be used for further attacks! No International obligation warrants unconditional cooperation at the expense of national security.” ​ The message also said that, speaking at the IAEA Board of Governors today, the Iranian permanent mission delivered a clear message: You cannot bomb nuclear facilities, continue threatening further attacks, and then demand detailed information and unrestricted access. ​ “Board of Governors must address massive military attacks on safeguarded nuclear facilities, and public threats of repetition. Otherwise, no credibility remains of non-proliferation norms,” the Iranian mission warned. 📲 @Irna_en ​
